published_statement: p.62-63: 'the contribution due to the complex valued function J(z) in F^S is negligible. Hence, to find the negative zeros we study the equation b0 + b1 gamma + b2 gamma^2 = 0 ... In Planck units, kappa^-1 is the squared value of the reduced Planck mass M_P, and thus b1 is much larger than the remaining renormalisation constants. Hence ... gamma~ ~= -b0/b1 = -16 pi G alpha~^S_1 m^4 and it does not depend on the choice of alpha~^S_3 and xi. Thus, the effective Hubble parameter of the predicted de Sitter spacetime reads H = sqrt(-gamma~), and hence we obtain the following value of the cosmological constant in Planck units according to the (semiclassical) Friedmann equations Lambda = 3 Omega_Lambda H^2 = 6 Omega_Lambda alpha~^S_1 (m/M_P)^4 M_P^2 ... Comparing this theoretical result with the experimental values of Omega_Lambda and Lambda inferred from the Planck measurements of the CMB [1], i.e., Omega_Lambda ~= 0.685 and Lambda ~= 7.15 x 10^-121 M_P^2, we obtain an approximated value of the mass of the field, that is m ~= 7.8 x 10^-3 eV.'
